What's new in 2.31.0

Clipboard History stops being a list of grey text — links show what they point at, code is coloured, and everything is filed under the day you copied it. The fullscreen image viewer learns to zoom properly, and Agent Watch shows what your sessions are costing.

Clipboard History ⌃⌥C

  • A copied link shows what it points at. The preview resolves it and shows the thing itself — the image, the PDF open at page one, the JSON or Markdown or source, a player for a clip, and for an ordinary page the title, description and picture the page offers to anything that links to it. The address stays above it, because the link is still what you copied.
  • The list fills in its own thumbnails. Opening the palette looks up the links it's showing, so a row has its picture by the time you reach it rather than only once you've stopped on it.
  • Code is coloured. JSON, JavaScript, Swift, Python, Ruby, Go, Rust, the C family, HTML, XML, CSS, shell, SQL, YAML and diffs. Dax works out which from the text itself, and leaves anything it can't name with confidence as plain text — prose is never coloured as code.
  • Grouped by when you copied it. Today, Yesterday, Previous 7 Days, and so on, so a long history has somewhere to aim rather than being one unbroken column. Pressing ↩ on an old entry now files it under Today, where it belongs once it's back on your clipboard.
  • A shorter copy sound. The old chime ran long enough to overlap with itself when you copied twice quickly. The new one lands and gets out of the way. Still off unless you switch it on.
  • Looking up a link is optional. It's the one thing in Clipboard History that leaves your Mac, it only happens while the palette is open, never when you copy, and there's a switch in Settings.

The image viewer ⌘F

  • Scroll to zoom, anchored on the pointer. Whatever sits under the cursor stays under it the whole way in — the old pinch-only zoom grew from the centre, so the thing you wanted a closer look at slid off screen on the way.
  • 10% to 1000%, and pinch anywhere. Zooming out past fit works now, and both gestures work across the whole panel instead of only over the image — which mattered most at the sizes where the image is small.
  • An open hand over the whole screen, closing to a fist while you drag, so it's clear the image can be moved.

Agent Watch ⌃⌥M

  • What each session has spent. Watching an agent work tells you it's busy but not what it's costing. The number climbs while you watch it.
  • Stop a session from the list. Both lists carry a stop button, and the palette takes ⌘⌫ on the selected row — no going to find the window first.

Also in this release

  • Annotate has a blur tool R — drag a rectangle over anything you'd rather not send. Arrows are softer, and lines start thicker.
  • Image to Prompt asks which style you want rather than assuming, and its result card gets out of the way when Generate Image opens on top of it.
  • The shortcuts board shows your version, so you don't have to open Settings to check what you're running.
  • Signed, notarized, universal (Apple Silicon & Intel), macOS 14+.
